industry.why: Neutral at industry level, carried, with the sector rows carrying the view. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): technology saw $5.5 billion of net selling in the week, the most since January 2025 (Jefferies, 17 Oct), the rotation came out of it, and Wood says 'the easy money in semis is made'; against that, Jefferies finds sector pockets still upgrading inside it (analogue chips, optical networking, artificial-intelligence memory) and Morgan Stanley still rates North American semiconductors Attractive. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: B now, B prior at industry level, carried by Semiconductors at A. The industry row stays C because the industry is split: Semiconductors (D), Software B2B Enterprise (D), Fintech (D) and Games (D) carry the Underweight; IT services, Hardware and vertical software stay Neutral. Counter-case for D: the heaviest net selling in 21 months is a regime statement; for B: the only industry with upgrades inside the sell-off.

memo.verdict: Progress the case to Early-Stage, with a price discipline. Bullish on the business, neutral on the shares at 1211p (2026-10-01). Accumulate below about 1160p, where the eighteen-month modal return clears 20% a year; above that, only on evidence at the H1 FY2027 results on 2026-11-09 that contractor headcount is falling and Workday Services like-for-like gross margin is recovering; do not chase the shares above 1250p. Conviction: medium on the thesis, medium-to-low on the entry. The park rule is not triggered: no D or F on management (RA 3, E 1, BB 4: B), business quality (E 2, BB 2: B), predictability (RA 8, E 2, BB 4: B) or trackability (RA 7, E 2, BB 4: C). The record's one-line summary of itself: the thesis is right; the price has got there first.
case: - A self-help case riding a demand recovery. The founder returned on 11 December 2024, restructured 190 roles within three months (£8.4m charge, March 2025) and within ten re-set the strategy toward £200m ARR by 2030 (Capital Markets Day 22 October 2025), prime-contractor roles on the largest public programmes, Canada (Davis Pier, 15 September 2025, £11.2m) and a dedicated AI business (Actonomy, 21 September 2026). UK public-sector digital procurement normalised over the same period after a trough that cut public-sector revenue 15% to £62m in H1 FY2025. The internal change decides what the company earns on the recovery; the recovery decides how much there is to earn on.

- The change has travelled all six layers on growth: resources (chief executive, rebuilt software bench), choices (strategy, the 18 August 2026 upgrade), actions (restructuring, contractor mobilisation, acquisition, products, £90m of buybacks November 2024 to May 2026 cancelling 6.9m shares), key operating metrics (bookings +32%, backlog +18%, ARR +23%, multi-product customers 41% from 35%), financial statements (revenue +17.4%, +27.6% in H2), sell-side estimates (FY2027 EPS +11.3% over three months, +15.3% over twelve, to 2026-09-25; no cut from any broker).

- The one output that has not moved is the margin, and that is the shape of the case. Adjusted pre-tax margin 15.6% from 17.9% because wins were staffed with 259 contractors (about 1 point of group gross margin). FY2027 guidance at consensus (£84.2m on £542m) implies about 15.5%, no recovery. Recovery is guided to H2 FY2027 (a clear margin improvement, no number), rests on timing (a contractor deploys in four weeks, a permanent hire takes five months; wage inflation moderated to low single digits) and on mix (Workday Products at 77.8% gross margin growing roughly twice the group rate adds about 0.3 points of group gross margin a year by arithmetic). First test: 2026-11-09.
counter_case: - At Building Block 1, the false friend, stated at full force: the bookings and revenue surge is real and profit never follows. Contractor dependence is structural, because public contracts must be staffed in weeks (four weeks for a contractor, five months for a permanent hire) and retention has slipped to 90%. Global systems integrators displaced from weak commercial markets have made 5% to 10% discounts the price of public work, took Kainos's DOS share from 10% to 4.6% over 2023 and 2024, and will follow Kainos into the larger programmes. The Workday channel has nearly doubled in UK partners (60 to 114) and the vendor's own Deployment Agent already cuts implementation hours by an estimated 30% with 50% in sight. Generative AI is passing 5% to 7% of delivery savings back to clients already. The evidence is FY2026 itself: revenue +17%, adjusted pre-tax profit +2%, gross margin -1.8 points, Workday Services gross margin -6 points, net promoter score -9, retention -3 points, and FY2027 guidance that at consensus (£84.2m on £542m) is a 15.5% margin, no recovery. On that path FY2029 EPS is about 63p rather than 70p, the multiple falls to the two-year median of 15.6x, and the shares are worth about 980p to 1050p, a 15% to 20% loss. The record concedes the whole of the FY2026 evidence, that the recovery is a forecast whose first test is six weeks away, and that at 19.3x the false-friend path returns roughly nothing over eighteen months, which is why the 'Modal return' is a C not a B. It holds the view because the top line is contracted not hoped for (£433.9m of backlog recognising 50% to 70% of contract value; DEFRA £150m alone exceeding FY2025 Digital Services bookings of £202m); because the mix shift to 77.8%-gross-margin software lifts group gross margin about 0.3 points a year by arithmetic whatever the services do; because the contractor cost has a timing cause and management showed in March 2025 it will cut cost to protect margin; because the fixed-price mix (37% of Workday Services, 20% of Digital Services) keeps the AI gain inside Kainos for now; and because even on the false-friend path EPS compounds at about 10% a year from revenue, so the hypothesis makes the case mediocre at this price, not wrong about the company. Where it bites is the price.

- At Building Block 2: Kainos's advantages are borrowed. Its demand is one government's budget, its channel is one vendor's goodwill, and its product moat exists inside a platform whose owner can widen the partner set, take implementations in-house, launch its own agents and change the fee. The partner count doubled; Workday GO and Flex Credits exist; the DOS share fell by more than half when integrators bid on price; the healthcare pipeline faces an NHS England reorganisation threatening 25% to 30% of anticipated healthcare business. The record concedes all of it and that the business has no pricing power beyond refusal; it holds because the dependencies are stable in direction over the horizon (Workday is moving services to partners, not away from them, on an eight-year agreement; the UK's digital roadmap runs to 2030), the customer-level switching costs are the company's own, and a company that has grown 15.8% a year for six years with these same dependencies has shown the expected change is plausible and probable.
triggers: - The H1 FY2027 results on 2026-11-09: the first disclosure of contractor headcount and gross margin since the update. Confirm: contractors below 259 and falling; Workday Services like-for-like gross margin above 47.7%, toward 50%; group gross margin above 46.1%; H1 revenue growth at or above 20% and adjusted pre-tax profit growth at or above 10%. Refute or alarm: contractors flat or above 259; Workday Services like-for-like gross margin below 47.7%; revenue growth below 20% or adjusted pre-tax profit growth below 10%. If contractors are still at 259, the market catch-up red flag is the first to watch.

- The margin path: contractors still above 200 at 31 March 2027, or a FY2029 adjusted EBITDA margin on a path to 16.3% or lower, is the drop-through world in which the rating falls to D or F and the recommendation to park. Two consecutive halves of margin recovery would change the record's mind the other way on the multiple branch. Utilisation below 70% and retention below 88% are alarms.

- Workday Products: ARR not crossing £100m by 31 December 2026 invalidates the software scaling thesis; ARR growth below 20% at constant currency in any half, or net new ARR below £10m to £12m a quarter, is an alarm. FY2027 results in May 2027: the H2 FY2027 margin shown or not, with FY2028 guidance.

- The multiple: a fall below 16.5x (about 1033p) with earnings unchanged, or Workday Inc below 3.5x EV/Sales, is the de-rating branch; any change to the exclusive resell or the $10m fee is the Workday alarm. The TSR/Valuation pin should stay a C until the price falls toward 1160p or FY2028 estimates rise (the FY2028 EPS mean above 59.1p confirms).
- Framework pricing: Digital Services gross margin below 35.6% or a lost re-bid on a core framework (DOS, DALAS successors). Existing-customer share of revenue falling below 82%.

- Exogenous: the autumn Budget (a possible pause in mobilisations); the NHS England disbandment and the healthcare pipeline (healthcare revenue growth turning negative); a second insider sale near 1200p would read as a signal whatever its cause.
